question.text: Under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations, the sponsor and manager of the AIF shall act in what capacity towards its investors?

answer.text: Principal-to-principal capacity with no ongoing duty after investment
Fiduciary capacity, with an obligation to disclose all conflicts as and when they arise or seem likely to arise
Arms-length capacity consistent with a commercial counterparty
Trustee-only capacity limited to safekeeping of assets

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Series XIX-C page 299, the SEBI (AIF) Regulations state that the sponsor and manager of the AIF shall act in a fiduciary capacity towards investors and disclose all conflicts of interest as and when they arise or seem likely to arise. The Trap: Principal-to-principal and arms-length framings wrongly remove the ongoing fiduciary duty. Trustee-only capacity is too narrow, since the trustee function is separate from the manager's fiduciary obligation. Note: Anchor the answer on the page 299 fiduciary-capacity-and-conflict-disclosure rule.
